events.title: Macintosh Plus released
events.summary: Apple released the Macintosh Plus on January 16, 1986 — the first Mac with 1 MB [RAM], a SCSI port, and the extended keyboard.
events.about: The Plus was the Mac developers actually used for desktop publishing and [HyperCard] stacks — enough memory to run MultiFinder and SCSI hard drives. It extended the Macintosh platform through the late 1980s before the SE and II arrived.

narrative.whyChosen: The Mac Plus made the original Macintosh platform practical for daily professional work.
narrative.whyImportant: SCSI and expanded [RAM] turned the Mac from a demo machine into a production tool.
narrative.problemSolved: Original Macs lacked memory and storage expansion for serious applications.

events.title: Brain boot-sector virus spreads on PCs
events.summary: The Brain virus appeared in January 1986 on [IBM] [PC] [floppy disk]s from Pakistan — widely considered the first [PC] virus to spread in the wild.
events.about: Brain infected the boot sector of 360 KB floppies and displayed a copyright message from its authors, Basit and Amjad Farooq Alvi. It launched the antivirus industry, boot-sector scanning, and decades of copy-protection versus malware debates — the [PC] equivalent of what Morris would do to Unix networks two years later.

narrative.whyChosen: Brain is the canonical first [IBM] [PC] virus developers cite in security history.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved removable media could propagate malicious code across the growing [PC] installed base.
narrative.problemSolved: Nothing was solved — it exposed that PCs had no integrity checks on boot sectors or floppy images.
